content: Ownership and use periods are assumed continuous from the entered dates to the sale. Reduced exclusions for a move caused by work, health or unforeseen circumstances (IRC 121(c)) and the once-in-two-years limit (IRC 121(b)(3)) are not modeled.

Mixed-use property (a rental with a rental-use share below 100%) divides rent, expenses, depreciation, carrying costs and loan interest by the year's rental-use share. On sale, gain up to the depreciation taken is unrecaptured section 1250 gain and always taxed. The rest of the gain is split by the month-weighted average rental share over the ownership period (from the ownership date, else the plan start). For a main home, months before 2009 count as personal use. This use-ratio approximation stands in for both Treas. Reg. 1.121-1(e) (a separate rented unit) and IRC 121(b)(5) (nonqualified use). The exception for periods after the last use as a main home (IRC 121(b)(5)(C)(ii)(I)) is not modeled. The personal share of a main home's gain gets the exclusion when the ownership and use test is met; the rest is taxed. A loss is ordinary only for the rental share.

The rental share is modeled as a separate rental activity under IRC 469. The IRC 280A(c)(5) limit for a dwelling unit the owner also uses as a residence (rental deductions capped at rental income) is not applied, and the vacation home rules of IRC 280A(d) and (g) are not modeled.
The five-year lookback for net section 1231 losses (IRC 1231(c)) is not modeled; a net 1231 gain is always taxed as long-term capital gain.

Passive income from activities other than the plan's rental properties is not modeled. Modified AGI for the special allowance is estimated from the projection's AGI before rental items; IRA deductions are not added back.
